name: Divisibility-antichain representations by smooth numbers
description: construct() -> 128 rows corresponding to targets 1..128. Every row must contain 1..30 distinct positive 2^a*3^b*5^c terms summing to its target; no chosen term may divide another. All targets require valid representations. Minimize the total number of summands over all targets, an explicit local refinement of finite d-completeness. Represent targets 1..128 by sums of distinct 2,3,5-smooth numbers forming a divisibility antichain. All targets require valid representations; minimizing the total term count is an explicit local efficiency refinement of finite d-completeness. The seed uses up to three terms and is not term-minimal.

state_of_the_art.statement: The minimum total is 220. Every target up to 128 needs at most three pairwise non-dividing 5-smooth summands, and an exhaustive search for each target (scripts/check_state_of_the_art.py) gives per-target minima that sum to 220. The d-completeness of such sequences was conjectured by Erdős and Lewin (Erdős Problem #123, now proved).
